title: Pandex – Official European Law for AI Agents, over MCP
lede: Pandex serves legislation and top-court decisions from the EU and several European countries, with every past version of each law, to AI agents through one API and an MCP server.

points: Coverage spans the EU, Germany, France, the Netherlands, the UK, Austria, Switzerland, Luxembourg and ECHR case law, refreshed nightly.
Each article keeps its earlier versions and the date each took effect, so an agent can cite the text that was in force.
A coverage page marks each court as complete or partial and explains the gaps, such as sources behind Cloudflare challenges.
The maker's post gives a keyless setup: claude mcp add --transport http pandex https://api.pandex.io/mcp
In beta it is free up to 1,000 requests a day, then €1 per 1,000 requests, with a bulk data feed from €1,000 a month.

points.text: The top comment argues raw statute text is not enough: legal AI needs retrieval that ties every claim to an exact paragraph, and it names European competitors.
Several commenters say statutes alone miss how law is applied; court rulings, and even permit refusals and waiting times, matter too.
One commenter raises timing edge cases, such as a law published after its stated start date, which Switzerland and Austria resolve differently.
A suggestion to hunt for legal loopholes with Lean drew a sharp reply that courts interpret laws, so they cannot be checked like programs.
Readers ask for more countries, with one pointing to a repo that already holds all Spanish law as markdown.
